name: dev-workbench
description: Skills, agents and commands packaged as installable Claude Code plugins.

plugins.name: engineering-paved-path
plugins.description: Eight shared engineering skills — backend and frontend architecture, security review, PostgreSQL table design, TypeScript type work, Mermaid diagrams, the four-level severity scale and the rule for discovering a repository's own commands. The single source other plugins depend on instead of copying.

plugins.name: research-tools
plugins.description: Two read-only agents for questions that need a checkable answer — a researcher that reports how something works or what the outside world says, with every claim addressed to a path:line or a URL it opened, and a cheap investigator that traces what connects to what.

plugins.name: architecture-review
plugins.description: An agent that reviews boundaries and nothing else — ring placement, dependency direction, ports and adapters, and the Server/Client line. Reads the repository's own architecture rules first and works where the automated gate cannot reach.

plugins.name: sdd-engineering
plugins.description: Spec-driven development as five agents and three skills — spec-creator, implementation-planner, implementer and plan-verifier, orchestrated by run-plan, with a retrospective, an insights recorder and the curator that keeps the insights store from growing past the point anyone reads it.

plugins.name: test-discipline
plugins.description: Tests for the change in front of you, in the framework this repository already uses — discovered from the nearest sibling test rather than assumed. Two skills and an agent, holding one rule: when a test and the code disagree, decide which of them is wrong before touching either.

plugins.name: change-docs
plugins.description: Everything a change needs after it works — annotated screenshots taken from the running page, a pull request description with a fixed shape and an explicit never-include list, and an agent that fixes the sentences a change made false rather than rewriting the documentation around them.

plugins.name: agent-authoring
plugins.description: Conventions for writing skills and agents, a static audit that checks a set of them still agrees with itself, and a local log for recording how an installed plugin actually behaved — which exports as a bug report, or as an eval case that arrives with its own regression test.

plugins.name: hook-guardrails
plugins.description: Two shell hooks that close two mistakes a prompt cannot reliably prevent — a push that lands on a protected branch, including the bare push whose upstream silently resolves to one, and a whole-repository format run triggered by editing a single file.

plugins.name: review-lenses
plugins.description: Reviews a change through only the lenses that change earned. Sizes the diff, picks the lanes from what it touches, dispatches them in one message so they actually run at once, sends every model-produced critical to an adversary that tries to refute it, and merges what survives into one ordered report.

plugins.name: refactor-safely
plugins.description: Cleans up code without changing what it does, by pinning the current behaviour in tests before any structure moves. Sorts every proposed change into apply, apply-after-reading-the-callers, and propose-only — and treats a characterisation test that fails as a finding rather than a test to loosen.
